FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: floating island
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_adj} whites whipped and poached in milk, set on a custard and streaked with caramel, with toasted flaked {2_coll}. The island floats because it is lighter than the sea.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chocolate mousse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted and bound with yolks, lightened with whipped whites folded in three goes — the first third to loosen it, the other two with a spatula, without knocking the air out.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: clafoutis
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} drowned in a {1_adj} and {2_adj} batter, baked until the batter sets around them. The stones are left in: they scent the whole thing with almond as it cooks.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poires belle Hélène
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} peeled and poached in a vanilla {2_adj} syrup, served cold under hot {1_coll} poured at the table. Escoffier named it after an Offenbach operetta.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: peach Melba
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached over vanilla ice cream, coated with a raw {1_adj} coulis — never cooked, or it loses its colour. Created for an Australian soprano.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pound cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: as much flour as {1_adj}, as sugar, as {2_adj} — four equal quarters, which is what the French name says. You weigh the eggs first and everything else follows.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: yoghurt cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the {1_adj} pot serves as the measure for everything else. The first cake anyone learns to make, and the only one whose recipe is never forgotten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: molten chocolate cake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} melted together, barely bound with flour, and baked very briefly so the centre stays liquid. Two minutes too long and it is only a cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: paris-brest
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a ring of choux pastry split and filled with a {1_adj} praline cream. The shape imitates a bicycle wheel: the pastrycook had his shop on the route of the race.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mille-feuille
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: three sheets of puff pastry baked under a weight to stay flat, built up with a {2_adj} pastry cream. Eaten lying on its side: nobody has ever managed it any other way.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coffee éclair
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a length of choux pastry filled with a {1_adj} cream and iced in the same flavour. The name is said to come from how fast it is eaten.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lemon meringue pie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a sharp {0_adj} curd beaten with butter, under a {1_adj} meringue piped in waves and burnt with a torch. The acidity has to stay frank, or the meringue flattens everything.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rum baba
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a risen dough dried out on purpose, then drowned in a warm {2_adj} syrup with {1_plur} until it can take up no more. Pressed gently, it should give juice back.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: profiteroles
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small choux buns filled with {2_adj} ice cream, drowned under hot {1_coll} poured in front of the guests. The clash of temperatures is the whole dessert.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: madeleines
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a batter rested in the cold then put into a very hot oven: the thermal shock makes the hump, and a madeleine without a hump has failed. Scented with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: financiers
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_adj} meal and {1_adj} whites, bound with {2_plur} cooked until it smells of hazelnut. Moulded into ingots, and once sold to the stockbrokers around the Bourse.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: canelés
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a liquid batter rested two days, baked in copper moulds lined with wax, until an almost black crust forms around a soft {1_adj} and {2_adj} heart.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dacquoise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: discs of {1_adj} meringue loaded with {0_adj} meal, dried in a slow oven and built up with buttercream. The biscuit has to stay crisp under the cream for hours.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Breton shortbread
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: almost as much salted {1_adj} as flour, barely worked so it stays sandy. The salt is not a seasoning here: it is the main ingredient after the butter.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: teurgoule
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} with cinnamon, baked five hours in the baker's oven in an earthenware dish, until a thick brown skin forms. The name comes from the burn it deals to anyone who will not wait.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bugnes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: ribbons of knotted dough, scented with {2_plur} and orange flower water, fried and sugared. Thick in Lyon, dry and brittle in Saint-Étienne: each city defends its own.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: calissons
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a paste of {0_adj} and candied {1_adj}, set on a sheet of wafer and iced white. The shuttle shape is said to date from a fifteenth-century comital wedding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: nougat
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {2_coll} cooked to the hard crack, poured over whipped whites and beaten for an hour, then loaded with toasted {0_adj}. Pressed between two sheets of wafer so it does not stick to the fingers.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sachertorte
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dense {0_adj} sponge, split and filled with a layer of {2_adj} jam, glazed with a dark smooth fondant. Two Viennese houses spent seven years in court over this cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: apfelstrudel
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough stretched by hand over a tablecloth until a newspaper can be read through it, filled with {0_adj} and dried {2_adj}, then rolled. One tear in the dough and it all begins again.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kaiserschmarrn
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick {1_adj} pancake torn into pieces with the spatula while it cooks, caramelised in sugar with dried {2_coll}. The Emperor's mess: the name admits its want of manners.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sernik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Polish curd cheese passed three times through a sieve, beaten with {1_plur} and baked slowly. Denser and less sweet than its western cousins.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: makowiec
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a brioche rolled over a mass of ground poppy seeds cooked with {2_plur}. The black and white spiral shows at the cut.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: medovik
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dozen discs of {1_adj} dough baked one at a time, stacked with a soured cream and left overnight so the whole thing softens and turns tender.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: syrniki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small curd cheese cakes bound with {1_plur}, fried in butter and served with soured cream and a {2_adj} jam.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cranachan
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} toasted dry, {1_coll} whipped with whisky and honey, {2_coll} crushed — layered in a glass without stirring, so that no two spoonfuls are alike.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sticky toffee pudding
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked and mashed into the batter, which turns it almost black, under a {2_adj} caramel poured hot and drunk up by the cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: banoffee pie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a base of crushed biscuits, a layer of condensed milk boiled to caramel, {0_coll} in rounds, and whipped {2_coll}. Invented in a Sussex pub in 1971.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: eton mess
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: broken {1_adj} meringue, whipped {2_coll} and crushed {0_coll}, thrown together carelessly. The disorder is the principle, not an accident.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bakewell tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a shortcrust base, a layer of {1_adj} jam, and an {0_adj} frangipane over the top that rises and browns in the oven.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tres leches
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a sponge dried out on purpose, pricked all over and drowned in three different milks until it can take no more. It has to be sodden without collapsing: that is the whole exercise.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: alfajores
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two very short biscuits stuck together with dulce de leche, the edges rolled in grated {2_plur}. They fall apart the moment you pick them up, which is the sign they are good.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: brigadeiro
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: condensed milk cooked with {0_plur} and {2_plur} until it pulls away from the pan, rolled into balls and coated in sprinkles. No Brazilian birthday is without them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pastel de nata
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an {0_adj} custard in a puff pastry shell, baked in a scorching oven until the top blisters black. Dusted with {2_adj} on the way out, never before.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pecan pie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} drowned in a {1_adj} and {2_adj} filling that sets as it bakes; they rise to the surface and form a crackling crust.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: brownie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: very little flour, a great deal of {0_adj}, and crushed {2_coll}. Out of the oven too late and it is only a cake; too early and it is not yet a brownie.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cheesecake
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a base of buttered biscuits under an {0_adj} and {1_adj} filling, baked in a water bath and cooled slowly — a shock of temperature splits it in two.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lamington
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of sponge dipped in a runny {1_adj} icing then rolled in grated {2_plur}. Australian, and named after a governor of Queensland who had nothing to do with it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: anzac biscuits
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} bound with golden syrup, no egg — they had to survive weeks at sea before reaching the trenches.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: malva pudding
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a South African {1_adj} and apricot cake, pricked as it leaves the oven and drowned in a hot {2_adj} sauce that it absorbs entirely.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: künefe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: fresh {0_coll} caught between two layers of shredded pastry, browned on both sides then doused in scalding syrup. Eaten at once: the cheese must still pull.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sütlaç
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked long and slow with {1_plur}, divided into earthenware dishes and passed under the grill until the surface browns in patches.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: maamoul
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a semolina worked with clarified {2_plur} and rested overnight, filled with {1_plur} and pressed into a carved wooden mould. Each pattern names a different filling.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: om ali
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: broken puff pastry drowned in sweetened {1_plur} and covered with {2_adj}, browned until the top crisps over a sodden underside.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: basbousa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a semolina cake with {1_adj} and {2_adj}, cut into diamonds before baking and soaked with syrup the moment it leaves the oven, while it is still scalding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gajar ka halwa
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} grated and cooked an hour in {1_plur} until every drop of liquid has gone, then candied in ghee. The vegetable becomes a dessert without anything else being added.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kulfi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} reduced by half over a low flame, scented with cardamom, loaded with {1_adj} and frozen in metal cones without being churned. Denser than ice cream, and slower to melt.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: jalebi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a batter fermented with {1_plur}, piped in spirals straight into the oil, then plunged for a few seconds into warm syrup. Crisp outside, soaked through within.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: taiyaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a waffle batter cooked in a mould shaped like a sea bream, filled with a sweet {1_adj} paste. Whether to bite the head or the tail first divides Japan.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hotteok
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a risen flatbread filled with cane {1_plur} and crushed {2_plur}, flattened on the hot plate. The filling turns into a boiling syrup that burns the tongue without fail.
